::: {.why}
The two costs you cannot see in any price series, which is exactly why they are the ones most often left out of a backtest and most reliably present in a brokerage statement.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Compute the annual financing and borrow cost of a long-short book at stated rates, and express it as a Sharpe reduction.
- Say what happens to the calculation when one name in your short book becomes hard to borrow.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Add financing to qlib/costs.py: a daily charge on the net debit balance at the broker call rate, and a daily borrow fee on the short market value at a per-name rate defaulting to general collateral. Apply it to your pairs strategy and report the drag in basis points a year and the Sharpe before and after.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Model the tail: assume 5 percent of your short positions become hard to borrow at 8 percent a year for a quarter of the holding period, and recompute. Then say what a recall would cost on top, using your day 12 notes. Borrow costs are not symmetric and the tail is what matters.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the assumption list for financing into the milestone report, since every number here is an assumption rather than a measurement until phase 10.
:::
:::

Your market-neutral book is 100 long and 100 short. What does it cost to carry for a year before you trade at all?
